key_insight: Routing codes are a new qLDPC family that keeps high encoding rates while making hardware connectivity shorter, simpler, and fully parallel.
engineering_relevance: They are designed to be easier to implement on superconducting and neutral-atom hardware by reducing wiring crossings, coupling length, and atom-movement complexity.
method: Construct a new family of qLDPC codes called routing codes.
Choose explicit instances with rates comparable to bivariate bicycle codes.
Arrange all non-local couplings to be mutually parallel to simplify hardware routing.
evidence_signal: Circuit-level simulations show weight-7 routing codes can reduce physical qubit overhead by about 8× versus surface codes at the same logical error rate.
watch_item: The result is promising, but practical benefit will depend on fabrication, control fidelity, and integration with a specific hardware layout and routing stack.
paper_title: Routing Codes: High-Rate Quantum LDPC Codes with Short, Parallel Non-Local Connectivity
